ratings.comment: Hist. 152: the exams are take home papers essentially, very long assignments.. the TAs are very tough graders as well. Her lectures just kind of seem like she's reading a script, so it could get dry. She's a cool person, tho, she focused on the history of LGBTQ a lot. There's just A LOT of papers in this class, zero exams/quizzes. Not my style

I have never done rate my professor before, but felt I needed to in order to warn innocents who haven't taken a history class. I have never felt more like I SHOULD NOT talk in a class. She corrects everything you say if it is not her opinion 100%. Her grading of papers is intense, as expected, but is insanely disrespectful. I felt I couldn't learn

Best Professor I've had at UW. She really cares about her students! She's also very funny. Take-home exams are very fair. If you go to class you will do well! Lots of reading but otherwise great class!

Really good class and professor! She makes the topic super interesting to learn about, and she's really passionate and knowledgeable. Reading and lecture are definitely a must if you want to know what's going on. Midterm and final essays are hard if you're not used to writing historical papers, but doable if you give yourself enough time.

She doesn't allow laptops in class so I suggest printing the outlines to make taking notes easier. Two midterms and one longer paper, which are easy to get good grades on if you go to TA office hours. Attend every discussion and most of the lectures and you will be fine

Johnson knows her job and material very well.  The Midterm and Final are hard (2 essays and ids).  Plus a longer paper on one of three books (choose first one).  She lectures fast with minimal visual aids.  TAs were great.  Did not help that it was an 8am class

Everything you thought you knew about the West is about to change. Prof. Johnson is great. You have to write a 6-page paper for one of the three books you read. You can probably get away with skimming the other two. You can miss 3 or 4 lectures, tops, but there's a few lectures that are way more important than others.

This is a reading heavy class, but it's interesting.  Professor Johnson has extensive knowledge about the American West and particularly minority groups. She writes her lectures ahead of time and reads them in class, meaning little interaction with students. The videos were good too.

Very interesting. Lectures get boring at times, but Easy to follow with lecture outlines posted the night before.  Hands out maps to aid the lectures which are essential for the midterm and final, which are both take home.  Just make sure to do the reading outside the class, as it pertains to discussion. Wish she discussed the reading more.

This is for History of the West (both sections).Easy to obtain high marks from this prof.  Simply spit back her interpretation of history word for word.  While every prof interjects their own views to some extent, this one does it AD NAUSEUM. Easy grades but what you'll learn is questionable at best.  And her book is HORRID.

Professor Johnson was amazing. Her lectures are fascinating and she presents them well. She does like to lecture formally, and expects a certain level of attention from students. Keep up with the reading and go to lecture and discussion and you'll be fine. She also chooses wonderful TAs. I absolutely loved this class! (Exams are take home too!)

Prof Johnson is the best professor I've ever had in any subject, and I'm an Animal Science major that hates history, so that's saying something. If you attend every lecture, read the books, and apply yourself you will get an A. She's a fascinating lecturer, a brilliant scholar, and her take on US expansion will blow your mind. Take her class!

Very work intensive class with lots of readings. Recommended if you love history/writing and are willing to work. Was much more work than other Hist 600s that I heard of. Prof. Johnson is a very nice person, extremely good with everything western history.

This lady is incredibly smart.  Clear lectures though they require a lot of writing.  Fascinating class, it's a great way to learn a lot about the US and our expansion - excellent class for ethnic studies. PS - I'm a business major, this is my first history, and I didn't feel it was over my head at all. Don't let the "461" intimidate you.

she is so nice.  Really enjoyed how she interacts with graduate students.  Wants you to do well, and she will help.  Very good at editing papers...useful to listen to if you need help with writing.  Would love to take her class again.

Great Professor. Can be difficult to follow along all the time, but that is because she is so passionate about the information that she just starts talking very quickly. Tests are take home, and there are only a few papers. Go to class, and make sure to draw IDs on maps, that is part of test. Take this class!

Prof. Johnson loves her subject and is very good at teaching it. I would recommend this class to any history major-- however to anybody who doesn't like to read, don't take it. There are between 100-350 pages of reading assigned each week with many papers. I loved this class, but if you're not in to working hard don't take it.
not a fan

If you're not a history major, be ready for a lot of reading!  My advice: find books that are already highlighted.  You will get the grade that you put into this class.  There are many opportunities for extra credit.  Prof. Johnson wants everyone to do well.  She has a very subtle sense of humor and is very passionate about her field.  Recommended!

This class is actually 4 credits so the courseload makes complete sense.  Lectures are ok, they can either be really good or really boring; take-home exams aren't too hard, you will most likely end up with a better grade than you think you will

Great class, material is very interesting and she supplements her intense lectures with videos/music/movies. More work than you'd expect for a 3-credit class, but you can get away with not doing all the readings since the midterm and final are take-home.

American Western History was quite possibly my favorite history class.  Take it! Take it now!  There is a lot of reading, but I really enjoyed it.  Prof Johnson also does a GREAT job picking out TAs, so that just adds to the awesomeness.

Fantastic class!  Learned more than I'd ever have expected to learn from a history class, being a non-history major.  Exciting, intriguing...there are thoughts from this class that I will retain for years and years to come.  Worldly even though the class was a Western history focus!
